key_results: C4-symmetric PLPP1 tetramer structures at 1.87 Å (apo) and 2.21 Å (product-bound); ordered lipid densities at inter-subunit interfaces; membrane-facing tunnel identified for LPA access
comments: High-resolution structures elegantly reveal lipid-organized assembly, though functional implications of specific interfacial lipids remain somewhat correlative rather than mechanistically proven.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Interfacial lipids stabilize tetramer assembly and regulate activity
hypotheses.result: Structure-guided mutagenesis shows activity changes, but activity loss does not simply correlate with tetramer disruption

title: MACF1 condensates serve as molecular rheostats translating mechanical stress into bone adaptation
task: Identify phase separation-driven mechanotransduction mechanism in bone cells
key_results: MACF1 undergoes mechanosensitive phase separation via IDR2; recruits PIEZO1, paxillin, and β-catenin into stress granules; MACF1-IDR2 delivery alleviates mechanical unloading-induced bone loss in mice
comments: Elegant linking of LLPS to mechanotransduction and in vivo bone adaptation; clear separation of condensate formation from protein interactions via arginine mutation validates the mechanism.

hypotheses.hypothesis: IDR2-driven LLPS is required for mechanosensitive cargo recruitment and bone adaptation
hypotheses.result: Arginine-mutated IDR2 separates interactions from condensation; MACF1-IDR2 delivery prevents mechanically-induced bone loss in vivo

title: A cryptic binding pocket regulates the metal-dependent activity of Cas9
task: Elucidate metal-dependent activation mechanism of Cas9 nuclease
key_results: Divalent metal-binding pocket (DBP) emerges dynamically at HNH–RuvC interface during activation; metal ions promote HNH domain activation and coupled catalytic activity
comments: Sophisticated multi-scale modeling (MD, Markov state models, QM/MM) reveals a cryptic regulatory pocket, providing mechanistic insight into how ionic environment affects genome editing efficiency.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Divalent metals regulate Cas9 activity through a cryptic binding pocket
hypotheses.result: DBP mutations disrupt HNH activation and impair both nuclease activities; quantum simulations reveal distinct catalytic behaviors among divalent metals

title: Power-law scaling of mitotic spindles with genome sizes across eukaryotes is driven by chromosome crowding
task: Explain mitotic spindle scaling with genome size across eukaryotes
key_results: Metaphase plate width scales with genome size by power law (exponent ~1/3) across eukaryotes, cell lines, and ploidy levels; chromosome crowding generates interchromosome pushing forces; spindle length independently regulated
comments: Elegant physical model and systematic comparative analysis reveal a universal scaling principle; demonstrates that chromosome volume rather than number drives spindle organization—a fundamental insight into mitotic geometry.

model_io.model: Mitotic spindle scaling (physical model + live-cell imaging)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Chromosome crowding forces set metaphase plate width independently of spindle length
hypotheses.result: Power-law scaling (exponent 1/3) of plate width with genome size; spindle length regulated by microtubule dynamics and cell size; acute spindle compression confirms crowding-force mechanism

title: Structural and functional insights into the recombinant PR-10 tomato allergen Sola l 4.02
task: Characterize structure and ligand binding of tomato PR-10 allergen Sola l 4.02
key_results: Canonical Bet v 1-like fold with conserved hydrophobic binding pocket; Tm = 57.5 °C; binds quercetin-3-glucoside, naringenin, and daidzein at low micromolar affinities; ligand binding increases protease resistance
comments: Comprehensive biophysical characterization reveals ligand-modulated proteolytic stability, with practical implications for allergenicity, though the functional significance of phenolic binding in vivo remains speculative.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ligand binding stabilizes Sola l 4.02 against proteolytic digestion
hypotheses.result: Naringenin and daidzein binding provide strongest protection; quercetin-3-glucoside shows low micromolar affinity

title: Increased mitochondrial biogenesis by GPR56 contributes to venetoclax resistance in acute myeloid leukemia
task: Identifying GPR56-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis as driver of venetoclax resistance in AML
key_results: GPR56 markedly upregulated post-venetoclax treatment; GPR56 activates RhoA–ROCK1–MAX axis upregulating PGC-1α to enhance mitochondrial biogenesis and counteract venetoclax-induced toxicity; GPR56 inhibitor DHM restores sensitivity
comments: The identification of GPR56 as a resistance driver is clinically relevant, though the study would benefit from exploring whether combination GPR56/venetoclax therapy improves outcomes in patient-derived samples.

model_io.model: AML cell lines and patient samples

hypotheses.hypothesis: GPR56 upregulation mediates venetoclax resistance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GPR56 inhibition restores sensitivity in resistant cells

title: ATF5 promotes redox homeostasis and cancer progression through nuclear-mitochondrial collaboration in pancreatic cancer
task: Determining role of ATF5-mediated mitochondrial quality control and MOTS-c signaling in pancreatic cancer progression and redox homeostasis
key_results: ATF5 overexpression correlates with poor prognosis; ATF5 activates UPRmt and MOTS-c–NRF2 axis; ATF5 depletion reduces MOTS-c nuclear translocation, exacerbates ROS accumulation, and reverses aggressive phenotype; exogenous MOTS-c alleviates mitochondrial injury
comments: The proposed nuclear-mitochondrial collaboration through MOTS-c translocation is intriguing but mechanistically underdetermined regarding how MOTS-c crosses the nuclear envelope and the specificity of NRF2 activation.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; exogenous MOTS-c alleviates mitochondrial injury in ATF5-depleted cells

task: Determining FOXP4-mediated redox homeostasis via SLC7A11 upregulation in suppressing ferroptosis in high-risk medulloblastoma
key_results: FOXP4 overexpressed in medulloblastoma, especially Group 3 subtype, correlates with poor prognosis; FOXP4 directly binds SLC7A11 promoter enhancing cystine uptake and glutathione biosynthesis; FOXP4 inhibition sensitizes MB cells and xenografts to ferroptosis-inducing therapies
comments: Mechanistically sound identification of FOXP4–SLC7A11 axis in ferroptosis resistance; however, the cell-type specificity of FOXP4 expression in the complex MB microenvironment remains unexplored.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; increased lipid ROS and 4-HNE accumulation in FOXP4-inhibited cells

title: An FXR-dependent cellular program for Kupffer cell pool restoration fuels liver regeneration
task: Elucidating FXR-dependent regulation of Kupffer cell homeostasis during liver regeneration
key_results: FXR promotes monocyte migration via Ccr2 targeting and Kupffer cell proliferation via CSF1/PI3K/Akt pathway; FXR-deficient mice show impaired Kupffer cell pool recovery and delayed hepatic regeneration after 70% partial hepatectomy

hypotheses.hypothesis: FXR regulates liver regeneration by maintaining Kupffer cell homeostasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; FXR-deficient mice show impaired immune cell activation and delayed regeneration

title: Periodontal pathogen Tannerella forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1⁺ neutrophil–dependent hepatic stellate cell activation

hypotheses.hypothesis: T. forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1+ neutrophil-mediated TNF-α signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ICAM-1 or TNF-α deletion attenuates fibrosis and inflammatory response

task: Investigating dysregulation of autophagy pathways in skeletal muscle atrophy during spaceflight
key_results: Transcriptomics analysis suggests involvement of alternative autophagy pathways in adaptive response to microgravity; basal autophagy dysregulation may contribute to rapid muscle atrophy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Alternative autophagy pathways are activated as adaptive response to microgravity
hypotheses.result: Suggested by transcriptomics; requires functional validation

title: In vivo DNA damage protection during cell migration across confining embryonic tissue environments

key_results: Neural crest cells under extreme nuclear deformation exhibit nucleo-cytoplasmic leakage without rupture or increased DNA damage; LaminB2 depletion accelerates recovery from deformation

title: Human adult and pediatric multimodal transcriptomic atlas of progression from pressure-loaded to failing right ventricle
